findings.description: SYS-SUP-033 requires the latch, per-code counts and fault history to survive software and watchdog resets. SYE-SUP-067 names the microcontroller as a placeholder, but no reset-retentive storage element or its reset and power-loss behavior is established. OP-SYE-001 records the missing hardware decision.
findings.requested_change: Identify and allocate suitable reset-retentive storage and its interface, supported by the hardware decision and reset-behavior evidence.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-015 requires fault-free start-up without a watchdog reset. OP-SYE-006 records that watchdog activation, first-refresh timing and integrity-check duration are not established, so the stated start-up sequence cannot yet demonstrate that outcome.
findings.requested_change: Resolve watchdog activation and timing using platform evidence, then specify a feasible start-up and refresh sequence.

findings.description: DEC-SYE-006 reserves half the 10% processor budget for software CRC and half for all other supervisor work, but OP-SYE-007 states that neither CRC throughput nor other execution costs are established. Feasibility of SYS-SUP-022 and SYS-SUP-052 is therefore unshown.
findings.requested_change: Establish execution costs and timing interactions and demonstrate that the per-cycle and one-second limits can be met.

findings.description: DEC-SYE-007 explains that a stalled or starved supervisor stops refreshing the independently clocked IWDG, but OP-SYE-008 leaves interference through shared processor, memory and data unanalysed. It does not establish that faulty application execution cannot corrupt supervision or continue watchdog refreshes.
findings.requested_change: Analyse shared-resource interference and allocate the protections or assumptions needed to preserve supervision and watchdog independence.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-053 and SYS-SUP-054 require fault injection and verification without the real board. OP-SYE-004 records that GPIO, serial, reset-flag observation and the necessary stimulation mechanisms have not been established in the named environments.
findings.requested_change: Identify and establish feasible observation and stimulation mechanisms for the required integration properties.

findings.description: SYE-SUP-052 now states that the CRC peripheral interface is conditional and accelerates software computation SYE-SUP-064, but its endpoints remain SYE-SUP-020, SYE-SUP-024 and SYE-SUP-004 and omit SYE-SUP-064. This conflicts with the described conditional connection.
findings.requested_change: Align the interface endpoints and associated references with the stated conditional acceleration path.
